people.name: Robert Clive
people.summary: Led the Company army at Plassey (1757); twice Governor of Bengal; won the Diwani (1765).

roles.title: Governor of Bengal
roles.appointedBy: Company council at Calcutta, confirmed by the Court of Directors
roles.howGained: after his victory at Plassey

roles.title: Governor of Bengal
roles.howGained: sent back to Bengal after Buxar to settle affairs

facts: Led the Company's forces against Sirajuddaulah at Plassey in 1757.
Governor of Bengal 1758–60 and again 1765–67.
Obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa from Shah Alam II by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
Set up the Dual Government in Bengal (1765).
Earlier made his name in the Carnatic Wars — the siege of Arcot (1751).
Was questioned in the British Parliament about his wealth; died in 1774.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

images.credit: Nathaniel Dance, (later Sir Nathaniel Dance-Holland, Bt) (died 1811) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Sirajuddaulah
people.summary: Nawab of Bengal (1756–57); defeated at Plassey and assassinated.

alsoOn.text: Sirajuddaulah becomes Nawab of Bengal and captures Fort William (Calcutta).

facts: Became Nawab of Bengal when his grandfather Alivardi Khan died in 1756.
Asked the Company to stop fortifying its settlements and stop misusing trade privileges (dastaks).
Captured the Company factory at Kassimbazar and Fort William, Calcutta, in 1756.
Was defeated at Plassey (1757) because his commander Mir Jafar's forces never fought.
Was assassinated after Plassey.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Mir Jafar
people.summary: Sirajuddaulah's commander who betrayed him at Plassey; made Nawab by the Company.
facts: His forces never fought at Plassey — Clive had promised to make him nawab.
Nawab of Bengal 1757–60; deposed when he protested against the Company.
Reinstalled as nawab in 1763 after Mir Qasim's fall; died in 1765.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Mir Qasim
people.summary: Nawab of Bengal (1760–63) who resisted the Company; defeated at Buxar.
facts: Made nawab by the Company in place of Mir Jafar (1760).
Shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Monghyr and tried to build an independent army.
Protested against the misuse of free trade passes (dastaks) by Company servants.
Lost at Buxar (1764) with Shuja-ud-daula and Shah Alam II and was driven out of Bengal.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Shah Alam II
people.summary: Mughal emperor (1759–1806) who granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal (1765).

roles.title: Mughal emperor
roles.howGained: Declared emperor in exile after his father was murdered by the wazir Imad-ul-Mulk (1759)
roles.howEnded: died at Delhi under British protection

facts: Fought against the Company at Buxar (1764) with Mir Qasim and Shuja-ud-daula.
Granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
Received Kora and Allahabad and an annual tribute of Rs 26 lakh.
Lived under Maratha (Mahadji Sindhia) protection and, after 1803, British protection at Delhi.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Shuja-ud-daula
people.summary: Nawab of Awadh (1754–75); defeated at Buxar.
facts: Joined Ahmad Shah Abdali against the Marathas at Panipat (1761).
Joined Mir Qasim and Shah Alam II against the Company at Buxar (1764).
By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) got Awadh back but paid Rs 50 lakh as war indemnity.
Accepted a Company force for Awadh's defence at his cost.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

images.credit: Tilly Kettle, 1735-1786, British, active in India (from 1769 to 1776) / Wikimedia Commons

roles.title: Nawab of Awadh
roles.howGained: inherited

people.name: Haidar Ali
people.summary: Ruler of Mysore (1761–82) who fought the first two Anglo-Mysore wars.
facts: Ruled Mysore from 1761 to 1782.
Defeated the British in the First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–69), ended by the Treaty of Madras.
Died in 1782 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War; Tipu continued it.
Modernised his army with French help.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Tipu Sultan
people.summary: Ruler of Mysore (1782–99), the 'Tiger of Mysore', killed defending Srirangapatna.

alsoOn.text: Tipu Sultan stops the export of sandalwood, pepper and cardamom through Mysore's ports.

facts: Ruled Mysore from 1782 to 1799.
In 1785 stopped the export of sandalwood, pepper and cardamom through his kingdom's ports.
Did not allow local merchants to trade with the Company.
Built close ties with the French and modernised his army with their help.
Ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War by the Treaty of Mangalore (1784).
Lost half his kingdom by the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792); two of his sons were held hostage.
Killed on 4 May 1799 defending his capital Srirangapatna.
Had a tiger on his flag; the British took his mechanical toy tiger (Tipu's Tiger).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

images.credit: Anonymous artist from Mysore, India. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Mahadji Sindhia
people.summary: Maratha chief and statesman; signed the Treaty of Salbai (1782).
facts: Fought at Panipat (1761) and escaped badly wounded, lamed for life.
One of the two famous Maratha statesmen of the late 18th century (with Nana Phadnis).
Negotiated the Treaty of Salbai (1782) that ended the First Anglo-Maratha War.
Controlled Delhi and protected the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II in the 1780s.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

roles.title: Head of the Sindhia house (Gwalior)
roles.howGained: Recognised as Sindhia chief after a succession dispute

people.name: Nana Phadnis
people.summary: Chief minister at Pune who led the Maratha confederacy in the First Anglo-Maratha War.
facts: Famous Maratha statesman of the late 18th century.
Led the regency council (Barbhai) for the young Peshwa Madhavrao II.
Held the Maratha confederacy together until his death in 1800.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Baji Rao II
people.summary: Last Peshwa (1795–1818); signed the Treaty of Bassein (1802).
facts: Signed the Treaty of Bassein (1802), accepting the Subsidiary Alliance.
Lost the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–19); the Peshwa post was abolished.
Was sent to Bithur near Kanpur with a pension.
Adopted Nana Sahib, who led the 1857 revolt at Kanpur.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: Nizam Ali Khan
people.summary: Nizam of Hyderabad (1762–1803); first to accept the Subsidiary Alliance (1798).
facts: Gave the Northern Circars to the Company by treaty (1766).
Lost to the Marathas at Kharda (1795).
First ruler to accept Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (1798).
Ceded the Rayalaseema districts (Ceded Districts) to the Company in 1800.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2 "From Trade to Territory"

people.name: William Jones
people.summary: Judge and scholar who founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784).
facts: Came to Calcutta in 1783 as a junior judge of the Supreme Court.
Founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal on 15 January 1784.
Translated Kalidasa's Abhijnana Shakuntalam into English (1789).
Pointed out the link between Sanskrit, Greek and Latin.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 6 'Civilising the Native, Educating the Nation'

people.name: Thomas Munro
people.summary: Developed the Ryotwari system; Collector of the Ceded Districts; Governor of Madras.
facts: Developed the ryotwari settlement, first tried by Alexander Read.
Was Collector of the Ceded Districts (Rayalaseema) from 1800 to 1807.
Governor of Madras from 1820; ryotwari spread across the Madras Presidency.
Called 'Father of the Ryotwari system'.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 3 'Ruling the Countryside'

people.name: Ahmad Shah Abdali
people.summary: Founder of the Durrani empire of Afghanistan; defeated the Marathas at Panipat (1761).

roles.title: King of Afghanistan
roles.howGained: Chosen by an assembly (jirga) of Afghan chiefs at Kandahar after Nadir Shah was murdered
roles.predecessor: Nadir Shah (as ruler of the region)
roles.howEnded: died; succeeded by his son Timur Shah

facts: Was a commander in Nadir Shah's army; became king in 1747 after Nadir Shah was murdered.
Invaded north India five times between 1748 and 1761 (NCERT).
Seized the Punjab and the Sarkar of Sirhind from the Mughals (NCERT).
Sacked Delhi and Mathura in 1757.
Defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) and then went home.
Faced strong resistance from the Sikh misls (Dal Khalsa) in the Punjab.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Sadashivrao Bhau
people.summary: Maratha commander-in-chief at Panipat (1761); cousin of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.

roles.title: Commander-in-chief, Maratha northern campaign
roles.howGained: Chosen after his victory over the Nizam at Udgir (1760)

facts: Son of Chimaji Appa, the brother of Peshwa Baji Rao I — so a cousin of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.
Defeated the Nizam at the Battle of Udgir (1760).
Captured Delhi (August 1760) and Kunjpura (October 1760).
Killed in the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Vishwasrao
people.summary: Eldest son and heir of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao; killed at Panipat.
facts: Was the nominal head of the Maratha army at Panipat.
His death by a gunshot around midday broke Maratha morale.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Balaji Baji Rao
people.summary: Peshwa (1740–61) under whom Maratha power reached its peak — and suffered the disaster of Panipat.

roles.title: Peshwa
roles.predecessor: his father, Peshwa Baji Rao I
roles.howGained: Appointed Peshwa after his father died (1740)
roles.howEnded: died in June 1761, soon after Panipat

facts: Son of Peshwa Baji Rao I.
After Chhatrapati Shahu died (1749), real power passed to the Peshwa at Pune.
Under him Maratha power spread to the Punjab, Bengal, Orissa and the south (NCERT).
Sent Sadashivrao Bhau north in 1760; died in June 1761 after hearing of Panipat.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Ibrahim Khan Gardi
people.summary: Commander of the Maratha artillery at Panipat; trained under the French.

roles.title: Artillery commander of the Maratha army

facts: Learnt modern artillery under the French general Bussy in the Nizam's service.
Led the Maratha guns at Panipat; captured and executed after the battle.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Malhar Rao Holkar
people.summary: Founder of the Holkar house of Indore; a senior commander at Panipat.
facts: Founded the Holkar dynasty of Indore.
Withdrew from the field at Panipat as the battle turned.
Grandfather-in-law of Ahilyabai Holkar.
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Najib-ud-Daula
people.summary: Rohilla Afghan chief who invited Abdali and controlled Delhi after Panipat.

roles.title: Mir Bakhshi of the Mughal empire (regent at Delhi)

facts: Invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to fight the Marathas.
Fought on Abdali's side at Panipat.
Ruled Delhi as Mir Bakhshi until his death (1770).
people.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II, Ch. 8 "Eighteenth-Century Political Formations"; NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Madhavrao II
people.summary: Peshwa as a child (1774–95); the Treaty of Salbai recognised him.

roles.title: Peshwa
roles.howGained: Made Peshwa as a baby — the son of the murdered Peshwa Narayanrao
roles.appointedBy: the Barbhai council led by Nana Phadnis

facts: Born after his father, Peshwa Narayanrao, was murdered (1773).
Nana Phadnis ran the government for him.
Recognised as Peshwa by the Company in the Treaty of Salbai (1782).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history

people.name: Raghunathrao
people.summary: Maratha claimant to the Peshwaship whose deal with the Company started the First Anglo-Maratha War.

roles.title: Peshwa
roles.howGained: Seized the post after Narayanrao's murder
roles.howEnded: removed by the Barbhai council when Madhavrao II was born

facts: Captured Lahore in 1758, driving out Abdali's son Timur Shah.
Suspected of a role in the murder of Peshwa Narayanrao (1773).
Signed the Treaty of Surat (1775) with the Bombay government for British help.
Dropped by the Company in the Treaty of Salbai (1782) and given a pension.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history

people.name: Hector Munro
people.summary: Company general who won the Battle of Buxar (1764).

roles.title: Commander of the Company army in Bengal

facts: Commanded the Company army that defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II at Buxar (22 October 1764).
Before Buxar he crushed a sepoy mutiny at Patna (1764).
In the Second Anglo-Mysore War he led the Madras army and retreated after Haidar Ali destroyed Baillie's force at Pollilur (1780).
Captured Negapatam from the Dutch (1781).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Jankoji Sindhia
people.summary: Young head of the Sindhia house; captured and killed after Panipat (1761).

roles.title: Head of the Sindhia house
roles.howGained: inherited

facts: Son of Jayappa Sindhia and nephew of Mahadji Sindhia.
Led the Sindhia troops at Panipat; captured and executed after the battle.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Dattaji Sindhia
people.summary: Maratha general killed by Abdali at Barari Ghat (1760) — the clash that led to Panipat.
facts: Uncle of Jankoji Sindhia; ran the Sindhia forces in the north.
Killed by Ahmad Shah Abdali at Barari Ghat near Delhi in January 1760.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Shah Wali Khan
people.summary: Wazir (prime minister) of Ahmad Shah Abdali; led the Afghan centre at Panipat.
facts: Was Abdali's wazir.
Commanded the centre of the Afghan army at Panipat (1761).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Lord Macartney
people.summary: Governor of Madras (1781–85) who signed the Treaty of Mangalore with Tipu.
facts: Signed the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) with Tipu Sultan.
Later led the first British embassy to China (1793).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: David Anderson
people.summary: Warren Hastings's envoy who negotiated and signed the Treaty of Salbai (1782).
facts: Sent by Hastings to Mahadji Sindhia's camp.
Signed the Treaty of Salbai for the Company (1782).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: William Popham
people.summary: Company officer who captured the fort of Gwalior (1780).
facts: Captured Gwalior from the Marathas in August 1780 during the First Anglo-Maratha War.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Jacob Camac
people.summary: Company officer who defeated Mahadji Sindhia at Sipri (1781).
facts: Beat Mahadji Sindhia at Sipri (1781), which pushed Mahadji towards the Treaty of Salbai.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Alivardi Khan
people.summary: Nawab of Bengal (1740–56); grandfather of Sirajuddaulah.

roles.title: Nawab of Bengal
roles.howGained: killed Sarfaraz Khan at the Battle of Giria and took the throne

facts: Seized Bengal by defeating Nawab Sarfaraz Khan at Giria (1740).
Fought years of Maratha raids (the bargis) and agreed to pay chauth (1751).
Named his grandson Sirajuddaulah as heir; died in 1756.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Henry Vansittart
people.summary: Governor of Bengal (1760–64) who replaced Mir Jafar with Mir Qasim.
facts: Deposed Mir Jafar and made Mir Qasim nawab (1760).
Failed to stop Company servants misusing dastaks, which led to war with Mir Qasim.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Najm-ud-Daula
people.summary: Nawab of Bengal in name (1765–66) under the Dual Government.
facts: Son of Mir Jafar.
Agreed in 1765 to let a Company-chosen deputy run the government; got a pension instead of power.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Madhavrao I
people.summary: Peshwa (1761–72) who rebuilt Maratha power after Panipat.

roles.title: Peshwa
roles.howGained: succeeded his father

facts: Became Peshwa at 16 after his father Balaji Baji Rao died (1761).
Restored Maratha power in the north within ten years of Panipat.
Defeated the Nizam and Haidar Ali in several campaigns.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Narayanrao
people.summary: Peshwa (1772–73) murdered at Shaniwar Wada; his murder started the succession crisis.

roles.title: Peshwa
roles.howGained: succeeded his brother

facts: Younger brother of Madhavrao I.
Murdered at Shaniwar Wada, Pune, in August 1773.
His posthumous son became Peshwa Madhavrao II.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Yashwantrao Holkar
people.summary: Holkar chief whose victory at Poona (1802) drove the Peshwa into the Treaty of Bassein.
facts: Defeated the Peshwa and Sindhia near Poona in October 1802; Baji Rao II fled to the British.
Fought the Company (1804–05) and made peace by the Treaty of Rajpurghat (1805).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Arthur Wellesley
people.summary: Younger brother of Lord Wellesley; won the Battle of Assaye (1803); later Duke of Wellington.
facts: Won the Battle of Assaye (1803) against Sindhia and Bhonsle.
Later became the Duke of Wellington and defeated Napoleon at Waterloo (1815).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Gerard Lake
people.summary: Company commander-in-chief who took Delhi and won at Laswari (1803).
facts: Captured Aligarh and Delhi (1803).
Defeated Sindhia's army at Laswari (1803).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

images.credit: Attributed to George Place / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Elijah Impey
people.summary: First Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

roles.title: Chief Justice, Supreme Court at Calcutta
roles.appointedBy: the British Crown under the Regulating Act

facts: First Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta, set up under the Regulating Act.
Sentenced Nanda Kumar to death (1775).

pairs.left: First Chief Justice, Calcutta Supreme Court

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2

people.name: Philip Francis
people.summary: Member of the Governor-General's council (1774–80) and Warren Hastings's chief opponent.

roles.title: Member, Governor-General's council
roles.appointedBy: British Parliament — named in the Regulating Act, 1773
roles.howEnded: wounded in a duel with Hastings; went home

facts: One of the four councillors named in the Regulating Act; with Clavering and Monson he often outvoted Hastings.
Fought a duel with Warren Hastings in 1780 and was wounded.
Argued for a permanent fixed land revenue — an idea later used in the Permanent Settlement (1793).
Helped bring about Hastings's impeachment in Britain.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Eyre Coote
people.summary: British general who won Wandiwash (1760) and beat Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781).
facts: Defeated the French under Lally at Wandiwash (1760), ending French power in India.
Defeated Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781) in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
Died at Madras in 1783.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: William Pitt the Younger
people.summary: British Prime Minister who passed Pitt's India Act (1784).
facts: Became Prime Minister at 24 — the youngest ever.
Passed Pitt's India Act (1784), creating the Board of Control.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Daulat Rao Sindhia
people.summary: Sindhia ruler of Gwalior (1794–1827) defeated in the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

roles.title: Ruler of the Sindhia state (Gwalior)
roles.howGained: adopted heir of Mahadji Sindhia

facts: Succeeded Mahadji Sindhia in 1794.
Lost at Assaye and Laswari (1803).
Signed the Treaty of Surji-Arjangaon (1803), giving up his lands between the Ganga and Yamuna and his hold on Delhi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Raghuji Bhonsle II
people.summary: Bhonsle ruler of Nagpur defeated in the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
facts: Fought with Sindhia at Assaye (1803).
Signed the Treaty of Deogaon (1803), giving up Cuttack (Orissa) and western Berar.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III
people.summary: Boy ruler placed on the Mysore throne by the British after Tipu's death (1799).

roles.title: Maharaja of Mysore
roles.howGained: restored the old Wodeyar dynasty after Tipu was killed

facts: Made Maharaja at the age of five under a subsidiary alliance (1799).
The British took over Mysore's administration in 1831 for misrule.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Saadat Ali Khan II
people.summary: Nawab of Awadh forced by Wellesley to cede half his territory (1801).

roles.title: Nawab of Awadh
roles.howGained: placed on the throne by the British, replacing Wazir Ali

facts: Could not pay for the subsidiary force; ceded Rohilkhand and the lower Doab to the Company (1801).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Count de Lally
people.summary: French commander in India defeated at Wandiwash (1760); executed in France.

roles.title: Commander of French forces in India

facts: Lost the Battle of Wandiwash to Eyre Coote (1760).
Surrendered Pondicherry in January 1761.
Was tried and executed in France (1766).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Marquis de Bussy
people.wiki: Charles Joseph Patissier, Marquis de Bussy-Castelnau
people.summary: French general who controlled the Nizam's court and got the Northern Circars for the French (1753).
facts: Served at the Nizam's court at Hyderabad from 1751.
Got the Northern Circars for the French (1753).
Taken prisoner at Wandiwash (1760).
Trained Indian soldiers in European-style warfare — Ibrahim Khan Gardi learnt under him.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Asaf-ud-Daula
people.summary: Nawab of Awadh (1775–97) who signed the Treaty of Faizabad and built the Bara Imambara at Lucknow.

roles.title: Nawab of Awadh
roles.howGained: inherited

facts: Signed the Treaty of Faizabad (1775), giving Benares to the Company.
Moved the capital of Awadh from Faizabad to Lucknow (1775).
Built the Bara Imambara at Lucknow.
His mother and grandmother were the "Begums of Awadh" whose treasure Hastings seized (1781).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

images.credit: Originally a local artist c. 1780 copying a painting by Zoffany / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Chait Singh
people.summary: Raja of Benares deposed by Warren Hastings (1781) — a charge in Hastings's impeachment.
facts: His zamindari of Benares passed under the Company by the Treaty of Faizabad (1775).
Hastings demanded extra money from him and deposed him when he resisted (1781).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra); NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2–3

people.name: Ranjit Singh
people.summary: Founder of the Sikh kingdom of the Punjab (ruled 1801–39); the Company did not dare attack him in his lifetime.

roles.title: Maharaja of the Punjab
roles.howGained: Chief of the Sukerchakia misl; united the misls, took Lahore (1799) and was proclaimed Maharaja (1801)
roles.howEnded: died; succeeded by his son Kharak Singh

facts: Captured Lahore in 1799 and made it his capital.
Signed the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with the Company, accepting the Sutlej as his border.
Took the Koh-i-noor diamond from the Afghan ex-king Shah Shuja (1813).
Conquered Multan (1818), Kashmir (1819) and Peshawar (1834).
Had his army trained by European officers such as Allard and Ventura.
The presence of Ranjit Singh held back the Company; after his death in 1839 two wars were fought (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Ch. 2; Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: David Ochterlony
people.summary: Company general who won the Anglo-Nepal War (1814–16).
facts: Defeated the Gorkha general Amar Singh Thapa at Malaun (1815).
Forced Nepal to ratify the Treaty of Sugauli (1816).
The Shaheed Minar in Kolkata was first built as the Ochterlony Monument.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Amar Singh Thapa
people.summary: Leading Gorkha general of Nepal in the Anglo-Nepal War.
facts: Held the western hills (Kumaon–Garhwal) for Nepal.
Surrendered to Ochterlony at Malaun (1815).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Buxi Jagabandhu
people.summary: Hereditary military commander of Khurda who led the Paika uprising (1817).

roles.title: Buxi (military commander) of Khurda
roles.howGained: hereditary

facts: Lost his estate after the British took Khurda and survived for two years on gifts from the people (NCERT).
Led 5,000–10,000 Paiks and Kandhs and seized Puri on 14 April 1817 (NCERT).
Kept up resistance until he surrendered in May 1825 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 (The Khurda Uprising)

people.name: Mukunda Dev II
people.summary: Raja of Khurda deposed by the British; the Paiks declared him their ruler in 1817.

roles.title: Raja of Khurda
roles.howGained: inherited
roles.howEnded: deposed by the British after resisting them

facts: Negotiated with the British to win back lands and the Jagannath temple rights; was refused after 1803 (NCERT).
Was deposed and allowed only to manage the Jagannath temple from Puri (NCERT).
Declared ruler by the Paiks in 1817; captured and imprisoned at Cuttack (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5

people.name: Mountstuart Elphinstone
people.summary: British Resident at Poona who defeated Baji Rao II, then governed Bombay (1819–27).
facts: Won the Battle of Khadki (1817) when the Peshwa attacked the Residency.
Ran the conquered Peshwa lands as Commissioner of the Deccan (1818).
Wrote a History of India (1841).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
titles: Raja (given by Mughal emperor Akbar II)
people.summary: Reformer who founded the Brahmo Sabha (1828) and campaigned against sati (NCERT).
facts: Founded the Brahmo Sabha, later known as the Brahmo Samaj, in Calcutta (NCERT).
Campaigned against sati; showed it had no sanction in ancient texts (NCERT).
Wanted Western education and more freedom and equality for women (NCERT).
Founded the Atmiya Sabha (1815).
Went to England as the envoy of Mughal emperor Akbar II, who gave him the title "Raja"; died at Bristol in 1833.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7 "Women, Caste and Reform"; Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rani Channamma
people.summary: Queen of Kittur (Karnataka) who took up arms when the British tried to annex her state (NCERT).
facts: Led an armed resistance when the British tried to annex Kitoor (Kittur) (NCERT).
Was arrested in 1824 and died in prison in 1829 (NCERT).
The British refused to recognise her adopted son as heir after her husband and son died.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2

people.name: Sangolli Rayanna
people.summary: A poor chowkidar of Sangoli who carried on Kittur's resistance; hanged by the British (NCERT).
facts: Carried on the resistance after Rani Channamma's arrest (NCERT).
With popular support he destroyed many British camps and records (NCERT).
Was caught and hanged by the British in 1830 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 2

people.name: Maha Bandula
people.summary: Burmese general in the First Anglo-Burmese War; killed at Danubyu (1825).
facts: Led the Burmese advance into Assam, Manipur and Bengal's borders.
Killed by a British shell at Danubyu (1825).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: William Sleeman
people.summary: Officer who led the campaign to wipe out the Thugs under Bentinck.

roles.title: Head of the Thuggee and Dacoity Department

facts: Led the suppression of Thuggee in the 1830s.
Later Resident at Lucknow; his reports on misrule were used to justify annexing Awadh (1856).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Thomas Babington Macaulay
people.summary: Law Member of the Governor-General's council; his Minute of 2 February 1835 made English the medium of higher education (NCERT).
facts: Wrote the Minute on Indian Education, 2 February 1835 (NCERT).
Saw India as uncivilised and argued for teaching English (NCERT).
Following his minute, the English Education Act of 1835 was introduced (NCERT).
Chaired the First Law Commission, which drafted the Indian Penal Code (enacted 1860).

pairs.right: English as medium of higher education

people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 6

people.name: Dost Mohammad Khan
people.summary: Amir of Afghanistan whom the British removed in 1839 and had to restore in 1842.

roles.title: Amir of Afghanistan (again)
roles.howGained: returned after the British withdrew

facts: The British suspected him of leaning towards Russia.
Deposed by the British in 1839 in favour of Shah Shuja; restored after the war.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Shah Shuja
people.summary: Former Afghan king put back on the throne by the British (1839); killed in 1842.
facts: Gave the Koh-i-noor to Ranjit Singh (1813) while a refugee.
Signed the Tripartite Treaty (1838).
Restored at Kabul by British troops (1839); murdered in 1842.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Print made by: Lowes Cato Dickinson After: Sir Vincent Eyre / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Charles Napier
people.summary: British general who conquered Sindh (1843).
facts: Defeated the Amirs of Sindh at Miani and Dubba (1843).
Is said to have reported the conquest with the one-word pun "Peccavi" (Latin: "I have sinned").
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Attributed to William Edward Kilburn (1818–91) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Duleep Singh
people.summary: Last Maharaja of the Punjab; deposed as a boy when the Punjab was annexed (1849).

roles.title: Maharaja of the Punjab
roles.howGained: made Maharaja at five after Sher Singh was assassinated
roles.howEnded: deposed when the Punjab was annexed

facts: Youngest son of Ranjit Singh.
Deposed and pensioned in 1849; the Koh-i-noor was sent to Queen Victoria.
Taken to England, where he lived most of his life.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Capt. Goldingham of London. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Rani Jindan
people.summary: Mother of Duleep Singh and regent of the Punjab; removed and exiled by the British.

roles.title: Regent of the Punjab
roles.howGained: as mother of the boy king
roles.howEnded: removed by the Treaty of Bhairowal

facts: Was regent for her son Duleep Singh.
Removed from power by the Treaty of Bhairowal (1846) and later exiled.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gulab Singh
people.summary: Dogra chief who bought Kashmir from the British by the Treaty of Amritsar (1846).

roles.title: Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir
roles.appointedBy: the East India Company (Treaty of Amritsar)
roles.howGained: bought Kashmir for Rs 75 lakh

facts: Served Ranjit Singh as Raja of Jammu.
Stayed neutral in the First Anglo-Sikh War.
Founded the Dogra dynasty of Jammu and Kashmir.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bahadur Shah Zafar
people.summary: Last Mughal emperor (1837–57); proclaimed leader of the revolt by the sepoys (NCERT).
facts: The sepoys forced their way into the Red Fort and proclaimed him their leader on 11 May 1857 (NCERT).
Tried in court and sentenced to life imprisonment; sent to Rangoon with Begum Zinat Mahal in October 1858 (NCERT).
Died in the Rangoon jail in November 1862 (NCERT).
An Urdu poet; "Zafar" was his pen name.

roles.title: Mughal emperor
roles.howGained: inherited

people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Mangal Pandey
people.summary: Sepoy hanged on 8 April 1857 for attacking his officers at Barrackpore (NCERT).
facts: A sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
Attacked his officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
Was hanged on 8 April 1857 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Nana Saheb
people.summary: Adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II who led the revolt at Kanpur (NCERT).
facts: Adopted son of the late Peshwa Baji Rao II; the British refused to continue his father's pension (NCERT).
Expelled the British garrison from Kanpur and proclaimed himself Peshwa, a governor under Bahadur Shah Zafar (NCERT).
Escaped to Nepal after the revolt; his fate is unknown.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Tantia Tope
people.summary: General of Nana Saheb who fought alongside Rani Lakshmibai (NCERT).
facts: Nana Saheb's general (NCERT).
Fought the British with Rani Lakshmibai (NCERT).
Waged guerrilla war in central India; captured, tried and killed in April 1859 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Rani Lakshmibai
people.summary: Rani of Jhansi who joined the rebel sepoys and was killed in battle in June 1858 (NCERT).
facts: Wanted the Company to recognise her adopted son as heir after her husband's death; it refused (NCERT).
Joined the rebel sepoys and fought the British with Tantia Tope (NCERT).
Was defeated and killed in June 1858 (NCERT), near Gwalior.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Begum Hazrat Mahal
people.summary: Wife of Wajid Ali Shah who organised the revolt at Lucknow (NCERT).
facts: Her son Birjis Qadr was proclaimed Nawab of Awadh at Lucknow (NCERT).
Took an active part in organising the uprising against the British (NCERT).
Escaped to Nepal after Lucknow fell.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Kunwar Singh
people.summary: An old zamindar of Bihar who fought the British for many months (NCERT).
facts: Zamindar of Jagdishpur near Arrah, Bihar.
Joined the rebel sepoys and battled the British for many months (NCERT).
Died in April 1858 after a last victory near Jagdishpur.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

images.credit: a steel engraving from 'The Indian Empire' / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
people.summary: A maulvi of Faizabad who raised a huge force and fought the British at Lucknow (NCERT).
facts: Prophesied that British rule would soon end and raised a large force (NCERT).
Fought at Lucknow; killed in 1858.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"; NCERT Class 12 Themes III, Ch. 11 "Rebels and the Raj"

images.credit: digital library of State Archives of Uttar Pradesh / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Bakht Khan
people.summary: A soldier from Bareilly who became the key military leader of the rebels at Delhi (NCERT).
facts: Brought a large force from Bareilly to Delhi (NCERT).
Became commander of the rebel forces in Delhi.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Rani Avantibai
people.summary: Rani of Ramgarh (Mandla, Madhya Pradesh) who led 4,000 soldiers against the British (NCERT).
facts: Raised and led an army of four thousand against the British (NCERT).
After an early victory at Kheri, chose death when surrounded (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Shah Mal
people.summary: Village leader of pargana Barout (UP) who led the peasants in 1857 (NCERT Class 12).
facts: Mobilised the headmen and cultivators of 84 villages (chaurasee des) (NCERT).
Was killed in battle in July 1857 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes III, Ch. 11 "Rebels and the Raj"

people.name: Wajid Ali Shah
people.summary: Last Nawab of Awadh, deposed when the Company took over Awadh (1856).
facts: Deposed in 1856 when Dalhousie annexed Awadh on grounds of misgovernment (NCERT).
Exiled to Calcutta (Metiabruz).
A patron of music, dance and poetry.

roles.title: King of Awadh
roles.howGained: inherited

people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 5 "When People Revolt"

people.name: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
people.summary: Reformer whose campaign led to the Widow Remarriage Act (1856) (NCERT).
facts: Used ancient texts to argue that widows could remarry (NCERT).
His campaign led to the law permitting widow remarriage in 1856 (NCERT).
Principal of the Sanskrit College, Calcutta; simplified Bengali prose.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7

people.name: Charles Wood
people.summary: President of the Board of Control who issued the education despatch of 1854 (NCERT).
facts: Wood's Despatch (1854) set out India's education policy (NCERT).

roles.title: President of the Board of Control

people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 6

people.name: Sidhu Manjhi
people.summary: Leader of the Santhal rebellion (NCERT).
facts: Led the Santhal rebellion of 1855–56 with his brother Kanhu (NCERT names him the leader).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes III, Ch. 10 "Colonialism and the Countryside"

people.name: Hugh Rose
people.summary: British general who took Jhansi and defeated Rani Lakshmibai (1858).
facts: Captured Jhansi (April 1858).
Defeated the rebels near Gwalior, where Rani Lakshmibai was killed (June 1858).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Colin Campbell
people.summary: British commander-in-chief who relieved and retook Lucknow (1857–58).
facts: Relieved the besieged Residency at Lucknow (November 1857).
Recaptured Lucknow (March 1858).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: John Nicholson
people.summary: British officer who led the assault that retook Delhi (September 1857).
facts: Led the storming of Delhi; mortally wounded in the assault.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: from "Forty-one years in India, by Frederick Sleigh Roberts- Project Gutenberg eText 16528 / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Salar Jung I
people.summary: Diwan (prime minister) of Hyderabad who modernised its government and kept the Nizam loyal in 1857.
facts: Became Diwan of Hyderabad in 1853.
Reformed revenue, justice and police.
Kept Hyderabad loyal to the British during the revolt of 1857.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Arthur Cotton
people.summary: Engineer who built the Dowleswaram barrage on the Godavari (1852).
facts: Built the Dowleswaram anicut on the Godavari (completed 1852), turning the delta into a rice bowl.
Also built the Prakasam-area works on the Krishna (planned) and Kaveri works.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Holt Mackenzie
people.summary: Company official who devised the mahalwari settlement (1822) (NCERT).
facts: Felt the village was an important institution in north India and should be preserved (NCERT).
His system came into effect in 1822 in the North-Western Provinces (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 3

people.name: Pusapati Vijayarama Raju
people.summary: Raja of Vizianagaram who, with the French general Bussy, destroyed Bobbili fort (1757) and was killed in revenge by Tandra Paparayudu.
facts: Raja of Vizianagaram who, with the French general Bussy, destroyed Bobbili fort (1757) and was killed in revenge by Tandra Paparayudu.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Tandra Paparayudu
people.summary: Bobbili warrior who, after the fall of Bobbili, killed Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram in his tent (1757).
facts: Bobbili warrior who, after the fall of Bobbili, killed Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram in his tent (1757).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
